title: Premier League Predictions: Arsenal Welcome Plucky Hull, Man Utd Host Aston Villa
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray7:00 AM ESTArsenal picked up a massive win at Liverpool last weekend.  / Carl Recine/Getty ImagesEnjoy Gameweek 10 of the Premier League campaign, folks, for there is another pesky international break on the horizon.

Fortunately, this club hiatus will last just two weeks, as opposed to the previous three-week break, but this is still the final opportunity to soak up English top flight action until play resumes on Saturday, Nov. 21.

There are some enticing duels on the slate, and it’s Manchester United’s critical battle with Aston Villa which headlines the action in Sunday’s late kickoff. Elsewhere, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur all face cross-country away days, while Arsenal return to Emirates Stadium for the first time in a fortnight.
With that in mind, here are Sports Illustrated’s predictions for Gameweek 10.

Friday plans certainly come better than Everton against Coventry City, an encounter which is unlikely to break any television viewing records or intrigue the neutral. But the Frank Lampard managerial derby remains an important fixture for its participants.

The Toffees will be motivated by the prospect of leapfrogging city rivals Liverpool in the standings, no matter how briefly, and an unlikely five-goal victory would even elevate them into the top four ahead of the weekend’s remaining fixtures.

Everton’s efficient approach will be tested by their former manager and his improving Coventry team, who have won three of their last five Premier League matches. A first meeting between the sides in nearly 26 years could see the Midlands side move even further clear of the relegation zone.

Tottenham Hotspur’s recent resurgence shows how quickly attitudes can change. Having briefly trailed the Premier League table, three successive victories—including a famous and rare win over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge—have lifted them to ninth.

Their expensive summer recruits are beginning to click, and the return of key players from injury has only boosted Spurs’ output. Seven goals across their three consecutive triumphs suggests Roberto De Zerbi’s side are starting to find their attacking groove.

However, Leeds United could easily halt their progress. While they are winless in five matches, they’re unbeaten in their four matches on home soil, with the backing of the Elland Road crowd propeling them to precious points. They could clinch a fourth stalemate of the season on their own patch during Saturday’s early kickoff.
Arsenal have won their previous four Premier League matches. / David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesPrediction: Arsenal 2–0 Hull

Following their staggering Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, reigning Premier League champions Arsenal have bounced back with characteristic grit. Their defensive masterclass facilitated a first win at Anfield in 14 years last weekend, and a rotated forward line proved the difference midweek as they overcame Slavia Prague.

Arsenal now sit at the summit of the Premier League once more following Man City’s recent blunders, and they’ve climbed to third in the Champions League’s 36-team table as well. They appear unlikely to be troubled by a spirited but ultimately limited Hull City side.

The Tigers have claimed a respectable 11 points from their opening nine matches, already stunning both Man Utd and Chelsea on their Premier League return, but this particular trip to the capital should prove a leap too far. Scoring a goal will be an achievement Arsenal’s watertight defense, let alone stealing a positive result.
Two of the Premier League’s most unpredictable forces under new management, Fulham and Newcastle United go head-to-head in the desperate search for victory.

The Cottagers have only managed narrow 1–0 wins over newly promoted sides in the league since Álvaro Arbeloa took charge, with goalscoring undoubtedly the greatest hurdle they must overcome. They’re currently averaging just one goal per game, with expensive center forward signing Gonzalo García having failed to score since the opening round defeat to Chelsea.

Newcastle will seek to punish their uninspiring hosts, although their form has also been underwhelming under Matthias Jaissle. Having lost three of their last four matches, they’re in dire need of a reaction as they struggle to cope with this summer’s enforced overhaul to their squad.
Man City must respond to successive league losses. / Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesPrediction: Nottingham Forest 1–2 Man City

Having been invincible during Enzo Maresca’s first seven Premier League matches in charge, Man City have suffered back-to-back defeats at the hands of the supremely organized Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion.

The Cityzens have underperformed during both losses, with even the division’s top scorer Erling Haaland unable to spare their blushes. Their play has become slow and sloppy, with a dramatic response needed against struggling Nottingham Forest.
